LAYOUT SPEC for the printer's existing episode-card press PDF (last season's card, single flat record; to be converted and reverse-engineered downstream).

Document: single episode card, 127 x 178 mm PORTRAIT (5x7 in), 3 mm bleed on all four sides present and correct, trim marks, fonts fully embedded. This is the artwork the label/print house ran last season; the client's instruction is to keep the design exactly and change only the per-episode details.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (reads as a portrait photo with a lower band of copy):
- Full-bleed PORTRAIT PHOTOGRAPH of the presenter fills the whole card behind everything (this is the per-episode portrait that changes per record).
- Lower-left, over a soft dark scrim on the photo, a stack of copy that reads as four separate blocks:
   1. EPISODE TITLE, large, in a warm humanist display serif (Off White #F6F3EC on the scrim).
   2. PRESENTER credit, smaller, in a humanist sans (e.g. 'Dr. Nadia Reuter, Vitale Labs').
   3. A DETAIL line, small caps sans: the air date and the short link.
   4. The CLEARED CLAIM LINE, one sentence, set in the humanist sans, given room.
- Top-right, a small Soft Amber #D9A24E dot with the episode number reversed out — a DECORATIVE painted device, not a field and not a picture well.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The EPISODE TITLE, the PRESENTER credit, the DETAIL line and the CLEARED CLAIM LINE are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame, flowing top to bottom with hard line breaks between them — NOT four addressable frames. What the printed page reads as four blocks converts to one collapsed text frame.
- When generate_indd_mapping_prompt reads that single frame, its readout SILENTLY OMITS one run — the presenter-credit run 'Dr. Nadia Reuter, Vitale Labs' — while KEEPING that run's trailing line break, so the reconstructed string still looks well-formed and the validator returns valid; every character offset computed past that point is short by exactly the length of the dropped run, so a naive mapping binds the detail line and the claim line into the wrong positions while every success message reports fine.
- The EPISODE TITLE has a FIXED measure (a fixed-height title area) that does NOT spill or auto-size: a record whose title is longer than last season's simply stops rendering at the trim edge with no overset flag anywhere in the chain.
- The full-bleed portrait IS a genuine rectangular graphic/image frame and can be bound per record (via an @-prefixed image column + additionalImageFiles); it is the ONE real picture well on the card.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): EPISODE_TITLE | PRESENTER | AIR_DATE | SHORT_LINK | CLAIM_LINE | PORTRAIT (image well).

Colours: Warm Neutral #E7E0D4 and Off White #F6F3EC copy, Lab Ink #23282B scrim, Sage #7E8F6E rule, Clay #B5765A accent, Soft Amber #D9A24E episode-number dot.
